runs.text: Where do we park Israel? You told me. We tried four spots. Episode three. Last time, Israel sailed out past Gibraltar, looking for a new spot. Spot one, from you: Russia's Jewish Autonomous Oblast. Stalin made it a Jewish homeland in nineteen thirty four. Today, eight hundred and thirty seven Jews <<ˈ|l|ɪ|v>> there. January averages minus twenty one degrees. The hummus freezes. Spot two, from you: New York. Easy. nine hundred and sixty thousand Jews already <<ˈ|l|ɪ|v>> in the city. One problem. Israel is about the size of New Jersey. And New Jersey said: one is enough. Spot three, from you: Indiana. Four Israels fit inside. The neighbours? Ohio and Kentucky. Biggest threat: corn. Spot four wasn't yours. It was Britain's idea, in nineteen oh three: land in East Africa. In nineteen oh five, the Zionist Congress said no, thanks. Then one of you wrote: park it where it already is. It's perfect. Jews have lived on that land for three thousand years. So Israel sails home. Millions of Palestinians call this land home too. Both peoples are staying. Where would you park your country? Tell me below. Episode four is yours. So tell me:
